## Question 1: Buck converter

```{python}
#|echo: false 
from lcapy import *
buck = Circuit(r"""
    V ._plus  0 {V_g  }; down
    M1 ._ND ._NG ._NS M1; up, kind=nigfetd, val=M1
    W V._plus M1._ND; right
    W M1._NG _gate_trigger; left, size=0.5
    ;;\ctikzset{bipoles/oscope/waveform=square}
    ;;\path (_gate_trigger) node[oscopeshape, scale=0.8, anchor=east](PWM){}; 
    W M1._NS X; right 
    D .1 X; up
    W 0 D.1; right
    W X L.1; right, i=i_L(t)
    L L.1 L.2; right, v=V_L(t)
    W L.2 _L2; right
    C _L2 .2; down, v=V
    W D.1 C.2; right
    W _L2 R.1; right
    R .1 .2; down, l^=R
    W C.2 R.2; right
    ; autoground=false, draw_nodes=connections, label_ids=false, label_nodes=alpha, european voltages,  """)
buck.draw()
```

Given buck converter with the following parameters:

-   $V_g=30 [V]$
-   $V_{out}=15[V]$
-   $P_{out}=60[W]$
-   $f_{s}=500[kHZ]$

Also, there are the following assumptions:

-   The converter is in CCM mode (the current through the coil always positive).

-   Both the transistor and the diode are ideal.

-    The output capacitor is very large, meaning constant $V_{out}$.
